outline.title: The Unpublished
outline.premise: In Santiago, Chile, 1973, investigative journalist Valentina Reyes obtains classified documents proving CIA coordination with Chilean military officers planning a coup against President Allende. As she races to publish her findings, every editor she approaches either refuses out of fear or is silenced by pressure from above, forcing Valentina to confront the question of whether truth has any power when every institution meant to carry it has already chosen a side.
themes: Institutional cowardice as a form of violence

characters.name: Valentina Reyes
characters.role: Protagonist — investigative journalist at a Santiago daily
characters.arc: Begins believing that documented truth is its own protection and ends understanding that bearing witness is an act of survival, not triumph.

characters.name: Rodrigo Fuentes
characters.role: Valentina's editor and mentor at El Clarín
characters.arc: Starts as a man who taught Valentina that the press is democracy's spine and ends having proved, by his own silence, that it can also be its coffin.

characters.name: Tomás Ibarra
characters.role: Mid-level CIA liaison officer posing as a U.S. Embassy cultural attaché
characters.arc: Moves from confident enforcer of institutional pressure to the face Valentina memorizes so that history will have at least one name to hold.

characters.name: Cecilia Vargas
characters.role: Valentina's source — a government typist who copied the documents
characters.arc: Risks everything to hand Valentina the truth and disappears before the story can protect her, becoming the story's moral weight.

chapters.title: The Documents
chapters.beat: Valentina receives the classified papers from Cecilia and confirms their authenticity, believing she holds the story that will stop the coup.
chapters.arc_notes: Exposition — ordinary world established: Valentina as a tenacious journalist who still trusts the press as an instrument of democratic defense; the inciting incident is Cecilia pressing the envelope into Valentina's hands in a market stall, shattering the ordinary and committing Valentina to the journey.

chapters.title: Every Door Closes
chapters.beat: Valentina takes the documents to three editors — including Rodrigo — and each refuses, citing fear, legal threat, or direct pressure from Tomás Ibarra, until Cecilia vanishes and Valentina is left alone with evidence no one will touch.
chapters.arc_notes: Rising Action through to Second Plot Point — obstacles escalate from professional rejection to personal danger; the midpoint apex is Rodrigo's refusal, the moment Valentina's last trusted institution fails her and she realizes the coup is not coming but is already structurally complete; the second plot point is Cecilia's disappearance, which strips Valentina of her source, her corroboration, and her last illusion that truth carries its own shield.

chapters.title: The Carbon Copy
chapters.beat: On the morning of September 11, 1973, as military jets circle Santiago, Valentina hides a carbon copy of the documents inside a wall of her apartment, choosing preservation over publication — an act of witness that costs her everything and saves nothing today.
chapters.arc_notes: Catastrophe — the coup succeeds; Valentina's transformation is made visible not through triumph but through the deliberate, quiet act of hiding the record for a future that may never come; survival-with-consequence: she is alive, the truth is buried in a wall, and the silence of every institution that could have stopped this is now permanent.
